 Culture Russia to replace Norway in ice hockey championship as more countries vow to boycott games
 November 8, 2026 3:18 pm  (Updated:  November 8, 2026 10:15 pm ) • 3 min read Prefer on Google by Yevgeniya Doluda Russian Olympic Committee (ROC) players celebrate goal during the men's play-off semifinal match against Sweden during the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympic Games, in Beijing, China on Feb. 18, 2022. (Anthony Wallace/AFP via Getty Images) The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association (NIHF) said on Nov. 8 that its team was dropped to a lower division at the 2027 World Junior Hockey Championship after news of Russia's reintegration into the tournament. 
 The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) paved the way for Russia's return to international ice hockey competitions after its Oct. 30 ruling made the International Ice Hockey Federation's (IIHF) exclusion of Russian athletes unlawful.
 After excluding Belarus from the upcoming tournaments, the IIHF said in a statement that it "continues to disagree" with the CAS's decision regarding Russian participation, but is "exploring all available avenues... to identify a constructive way forward that serves the interests of global ice hockey."
 "This clearly shows all the practical challenges and immediate consequences for everyone involved when countries are to be reinstated immediately," said NIHF Secretary General Petter Salsten in the association's statement about moving to a lower division at Russia's expense.
 In the new layout at the championship, which is due to take place in Canada from Dec. 26, 2026, to Jan. 5, 2027, Russia will place tenth. As the lowest-ranked team, Norway will move down to Division 1A.
 Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said during a press conference that "Russians will not be there" for the World Junior Hockey Championship, with the government later adding that its immigration minister, Lena Metlege Diab, "will exercise her authorities… to individually assess and prevent Russian and Belarusian athletes and officials from entering Canada to compete under their national symbols."
 The host country has yet to comment on these latest developments.
 Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha condemned the decision and called for a boycott of Russia's participation in the championship. 
 "International sports bureaucrats who make decisions about the return of Russians to international competitions are staining themselves with blood and becoming accomplices in Russian war crimes," he said on Nov. 8. 
 Sybiha said Kyiv stands in solidarity with Norway and urged international partners to withhold funding from the IIHF due to the "shameful decision."
 "Sport should never be used to legitimize an aggressor," he said. "Russia has no place on the ice as long as its barbaric war against Ukraine continues."
 A number of national hockey organizations have already sided with Ukraine. 
 The Swiss Ice Hockey Federation (SIHF) said that "in view of the ongoing conflict in Ukraine and the current circumstances, the Swiss U20 national team will not compete against the Russian U20 national team at the upcoming World Championship. "
 Switzerland is the latest country expressing its refusal to play games against Russia. 
 National hockey federations in Czechia, Finland, Canada, and elsewhere have sided with Ukraine. 
 Germany, however, has dropped threats to withdraw from hosting the championship tournament. 
 "We want to hold the world championship in Germany next year, and I am also very optimistic that we will manage that," German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) chief executive Frank Lutz told reporters on Nov. 8, according to the German Press Agency.
 The German hockey federation previously issued a statement saying that Russia's participation in the tournament would have "significant consequences in terms of security."
 "Some say that sports are separate from politics, but that's not true as long as missiles are destroying ice arenas and killing athletes," Ihor Merezhko, the captain of Ukraine's national men's team, told the Kyiv Independent.
 Russian and Belarusian teams have been excluded from IIHF competitions since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and Belarus supported the war.

 8:44 pm War Ukraine war latest: Ukraine hits key bridge on 'highway of death' linking mainland Russia to occupied regions 
 7:39 pm Ukrainian drones hit key bridge, power stations in Russia's Rostov Oblast, governor says. Drone debris reportedly damaged the bridge over the Mius River, located on the R-280 highway — a strategic road that links Rostov Oblast with several Russian-occupied regions in Ukraine, including Crimea. 
 6:18 pm Zelensky tasks PM with creating free transportation program in Kyiv as Russia's bridge attacks hinder travel. According to the president's advisor, Dmytro Lytvyn, the plan's details could be presented as soon as tomorrow.
 5:01 pm 3 people, including child, die in Kyiv Oblast from improperly running generator as Russia slams power grids across Ukraine. The State Emergency Service said the victims died of carbon monoxide poisoning because they ran the generator in the basement instead of outside, at a safe distance. Another child in the home was hospitalized following the incident.
 4:22 pm Why this South African decided to build a life in Ukraine — and document it. Kyiv-based South African tech entrepreneur and filmmaker Ronnie Apteker discusses Ukraine’s image abroad, persistent stereotypes, war fatigue, and the importance of telling stories that show Ukrainians as people building businesses, raising families, and creating despite the war.
 4:15 pm Europe to participate in Abu Dhabi peace talks, French foreign minister says. "The Europeans will be well represented, and France will be in Abu Dhabi to take part in these discussions. I cannot yet tell you who will represent France on this occasion, but it will certainly be there," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said.
 12:47 pm Moscow police detain over 200 people, reportedly forcing some to sign military contracts. Detainees told the Russian Telegram channel "Ostorozhno, Novosti" that those over the age of 18 were "persistently" urged to sign a contract with Russia's Defense Ministry. Reports of police beating the detainees, smashing their phones, and prohibiting them from using the toilet later emerged.
 10:59 am Russian attacks kill 8, injure 19 in Ukraine over the past day, striking Zaporizhzhia Oblast over 700 times. Russian forces carried out 725 strikes on 53 settlements in Zaporizhzhia Oblast alone, injuring one person, Governor Ivan Fedorov said. 
 9:29 am General Staff: Russia has lost 1,606,400 troops in Ukraine since Feb. 24, 2022 The number includes 2,290 casualties that Russian forces suffered over the past day.
 7:11 am Zelensky says more SBU personnel decisions coming after senior officials dismissed over criminal gang involvement. "Unfortunately, this week brought very different news about the SBU – frankly, disturbing, truly disgraceful, absolutely unacceptable things," President Volodymyr Zelensky said.
 3:59 am Senator Blumenthal to introduce legislation supporting Ukraine, calls for new US negotiators, Starlink controls. "Trump needs new negotiators—not fawning pawns who call this brutal murderer a 'humanitarian.' Congress must lead without delay," Sen. Richard Blumenthal said.
 Saturday , November 7 11:58 pm Russia to send senior diplomats, military officials to upcoming peace talks in Abu Dhabi. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov, who oversees Russia's relations with the United States and arms control issues, will join the negotiations for the first time.
 11:31 pm Belarus barred from 2027 ice hockey championships as IIHF weighs Russia's return after court ruling. Separately, the IIHF said it "continues to disagree" with an Oct. 30 ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) that overturned its exclusion of Russian teams from international competitions.
 9:40 pm Hackers claim leaked Russian data reveals up to 450,000 war-related deaths in Ukraine. The groups said they obtained the records from Rosstat's internal Demography database, containing information from death certificates registered between February 2022 and August 2026.
